name: GoFundMe Charity
description: GoFundMe Charity was GoFundMe's dedicated nonprofit fundraising brand. GoFundMe now offers nonprofit pages and supporter-led charity fundraisers on its main platform, while nonprofit administration and its full nonprofit fundraising product live in GoFundMe Pro, formerly Classy.
agentUseSummary: GoFundMe Charity cannot be installed as a separate Relay connector because the legacy brand no longer has an independent product or API authority. Its old domain redirects to GoFundMe's current nonprofit page, and the only current public nonprofit developer contract is explicitly GoFundMe Pro; Relay must evaluate that canonical Classy/GoFundMe Pro provider instead of creating duplicate connection state under this retired name.

blocked.label: Connect GoFundMe Charity
blocked.description: The legacy GoFundMe Charity brand has no independent current connection contract; creating one would duplicate current GoFundMe Pro/Classy authority.

blocked.label: Use the GoFundMe Pro API under the legacy name
blocked.description: Relay does not mount GoFundMe Pro OAuth, organizations, campaigns, transactions or supporter data under a second GoFundMe Charity identity.

blocked.label: Use private GoFundMe endpoints
blocked.description: GoFundMe's current public nonprofit-page materials do not publish a separate general GoFundMe charity-account API, and Relay does not reverse engineer private application traffic.

blocked.label: Automate GoFundMe charity administration
blocked.description: Relay does not collect GoFundMe passwords, impersonate verified nonprofit representatives or automate private charity and GoFundMe Pro dashboards.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No action is exposed for this retired duplicate brand; current GoFundMe Pro/Classy integration work belongs to its canonical provider.

runtimeSupport.description: The retired GoFundMe Charity identity has no separate current API surface to mount as OpenClaw tools.
The retired GoFundMe Charity identity has no separate current API surface to mount as Hermes tools.

providerSetup.blocker: The former charity.gofundme.com product identity redirects to GoFundMe's current nonprofit offering. GoFundMe states that verified nonprofit pages and their data are administered within GoFundMe Pro, and its only current public nonprofit API documentation is branded GoFundMe Pro; GoFundMe's terms identify that product as formerly Classy. A separate GoFundMe Charity connector would therefore duplicate the canonical Classy/GoFundMe Pro authority and could bind users to the wrong product or credential contract.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request credentials or show a separate GoFundMe Charity card. Complete and use the canonical Classy/GoFundMe Pro provider for its documented API. Reconsider this identity only if GoFundMe publishes a distinct customer-authorized API for main-platform nonprofit pages that is separate from GoFundMe Pro.

evidence.supports: The former GoFundMe Charity domain redirects to GoFundMe's current nonprofit fundraising page rather than exposing an independent legacy product or developer surface.

GoFundMe's current nonprofit page says claimed Nonprofit Pages and their donor/activity data are administered within GoFundMe Pro and presents GoFundMe Pro as its robust nonprofit fundraising platform.
GoFundMe's current public nonprofit API is explicitly the GoFundMe Pro API, with OAuth 2.0 and JSON resource endpoints; it is not documented as a separate GoFundMe Charity contract.
GoFundMe's current terms distinguish the main GoFundMe platform from GoFundMe Pro and identify GoFundMe Pro as formerly Classy, confirming the canonical current product identity.

GoFundMe documents current nonprofit fundraising, payment and payout behavior through the main platform, PayPal Giving Fund and GoFundMe Pay, while publishing no separate customer-callable GoFundMe Charity account API.
